newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal seen rejecting 10-yr bond bids.
newsitem.headline: Portugal seen rejecting 10-yr bond bids.

text.p: The recent instability in the bond markets will push banks to raise their bids at Portugal's Institute of Public Credit Management's (IGPC) auction of 25 billion escudos of 10-year bonds, analysts said.
They said the Institute was unlikely to accept such higher yields. The results of the auction for the February 2007 paper will be released around 1100 GMT.
"With this instability, the IGCP is unlikely to place anything because the proposed yields are going to rise significantly from the last auction," said one fixed-income trader.
Traders saw banks bidding at between 6.85 and 6.95 percent, with some bids even above seven percent, against the average 6.699 percent at the last such sale on February 14.

Traders said that the Institute would be unwilling to accept bids at or above the current secondary market level of 6.765 percent because that would be seen as sanctioning the sharp rise of the past couple of sessions.
The Portuguese secondary market yields were below the real level of the market because of a total lack of liquidity at the moment, traders said.
They noted that the Institute rejected bids at its offer of 182-day bills on Monday.
